summary: Increased 429 throttling during peak hours in us-east (queue depth / saturation suspected)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports elevated HTTP 429 responses (throttling) during peak traffic windows in us-east on a Dedicated pool.
- Symptom: sudden increase in 429 rate coincident with daily peak; request volume remains within contracted QPS but bursts trigger sustained throttling.

Impact
- Customer-facing request failures for chat completions.
- Approx. 4.8% of requests returned 429 between 17:05–18:20 ET (daily peak window).
- Customer reports downstream retry storms and increased end-user latency.

Customer-provided details (sanitized)
- Workload: chat completions, streaming enabled.
- Concurrency: peak burst ~220–260 concurrent requests.
- Their client retries 429 with exponential backoff (up to 4 retries).

Environment
- Dedicated capacity: us-east (single region).
- Models: rw-chat-13b primary, rw-instruct-70b for select routes.
- Routing policy: pinned to dedicated pool; no cross-region fallback.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Replay a representative burst profile on the dedicated pool (synthetic) for 10 minutes.
2) Observe scheduler queue depth and 429 counters on the gateway.
3) Validate whether 429s are rate-limit policy driven vs capacity/scheduler driven.

Initial hypothesis
- Dedicated pool saturation during bursty traffic leads to scheduler queue growth and gateway throttling.
- Potential contributing factors:
  - Queue depth threshold too aggressive for this customer’s traffic shape.
  - Missing/incorrect saturation telemetry (GPU queue depth / scheduler contention) making it hard to confirm quickly.
  - Retry amplification: 429s drive extra load, extending the saturation window.

Requested from customer
- A 30-minute window with timestamps of peak failures.
- One request-id sample and their per-minute request rate chart (no payloads).
investigation_notes:
Triage checklist
- Confirmed 429 source: api-gateway throttle (not upstream 5xx). Gateway reason tag: THROTTLED_POOL_SATURATION.
- Correlated with dedicated scheduler metrics: queue depth spikes align with 429 increase.

Key observations (us-east dedicated pool)
- Scheduler queue depth (p95) increased from ~15 to ~190 during 17:05–18:20 ET.
- Scheduler contention indicator (threads runnable / blocked time) rose materially during same window.
- GPU utilization looked “normal” (~55–70%) but SM occupancy and queue depth suggest the runtime was not the bottleneck; scheduler admission/dispatch was.
- KV cache pressure increased for rw-instruct-70b route (higher context lengths), increasing per-request service time and reducing effective throughput.

Telemetry gaps encountered (feeds into Reliability Program)
- Queue depth metric labels inconsistent across clusters; some series missing region/service labels, complicating per-pool drill-down.
- No single “saturation snapshot” panel for on-call; required hopping across 3 dashboards.
- Lack of consistent alerting on: queue depth + throttle rate + scheduler contention combination.

Actions taken during investigation
- Worked with Telemetry (Logan Wright) to validate the metric pipeline for queue depth and throttle counters in us-east.
- Verified rate-limit policy: customer not exceeding contractual QPS; throttles triggered by pool admission control based on queue depth.

Artifacts
- Internal incident thread: #incidents (INC-2025-02-18-UE1-THROTTLE) includes timeline, graphs, and mitigation discussion.
- This ticket’s findings captured as requirements for saturation collector v1 (bot context bundle) and saturation signal standardization.
resolution:
Customer-facing resolution
- Implemented temporary mitigation on customer’s dedicated pool in us-east:
  - Increased burst headroom (scheduler admission control thresholds) while maintaining safety limits.
  - Enabled safer retry guidance: customer updated client to cap concurrent retries to reduce amplification.
- Added/updated dashboards for this pool:
  - New panels for queue depth, throttling rate, and scheduler contention aligned to the saturation signal standard.

Outcome
- 429 rate returned to baseline (<0.2%) during the next two peak windows (validated 2025-02-20 and 2025-02-21).
- Customer confirmed end-user errors resolved; residual latency improved once retries reduced.

Follow-ups (internal)
- Feed learnings into incident bot saturation collector requirements:
  - Include queue depth, throttling, scheduler contention, KV cache pressure in the first bundle.
  - Ensure collector is region/pool aware and highlights missing telemetry explicitly.
- Observability remediation:
  - Normalize saturation metric labels and add cardinality guardrails.
  - Add an alert recipe for “sustained queue depth + throttles + contention” (dedicated pools).

Note: No customer data/payloads were captured or shared in internal channels; all logs referenced are aggregate counters and request IDs.
